newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney sees lower U.S. cold threat next week. [CORRECTED 20:16 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney sees lower U.S. cold threat next week. [CORRECTED 20:16 GMT]

text.p: A cold airmass that will move into the central United States during the middle of next week does not look to be as strong nor as big as earlier projected, Smith Barney meteorologists said Friday.

The northern Plains will still see cold weather by Wednesday, but a surface low will not be present to pull down the airmass from Canada, said Basilio Lopez, assistant to Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis.
"Heating demand, although still above normal levels, will not be as high as expected," Lopez said in Smith Barney's daily weather outlook.

The Midwest, which will still see the greatest temperature anomalies, will still see temperatures in the range of six to 12 degrees Farenheit below normal, rather than the 12 to 15 degrees below normal that was originally forecast.
Instead of seeing temperatures eight to 12 degrees below zero F during the latter part of the week, the Northeast will see readings of four to eight degrees below normal (corrects from zero).
"With the change in the energy forecast above, it is safe to say that Florida will avoid another frost or freeze event," Lopez said.
